chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who prays the prayer or performs ablution, then doubts regarding it afterwards, so he says: 'If I repeat the prayer or repeat the ablution, my wife will be unto me like the back of my mother,' and he swears upon that with divorce. He said: 'This is from the footsteps of Satan; there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.الزَّهْر: Zihar, likening one's wife to one's mother in terms of prohibition of intimacy
key_terms.خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ: Footsteps of Satan, referring to subtle whispers or doubts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar if it is vowed due to doubt in prayer or ablution?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling to illustrate how excessive doubt (shakk) in acts of worship can be exploited by Satan to create unnecessary religious burdens. The Imam clarifies that since the doubt is in the prayer or ablution itself, the conditional vow of Zihar is not triggered, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in jurisprudence when doubt is prevalent. This highlights the distinction between intentional declaration and doubt-induced uncertainty in marital vows.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who Prayed the Prayer, or performed ablution, so he doubted with regards to it after that, so he is saying that if he were to repeat his Prayer or repeat his ablution, so his wife would be unto him like the back of his mother, and he swears upon that with the divorce’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is from the footsteps of the Satan<sup>la</sup>. There is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who doubts a great deal in his wudu. He then says, ‘If I repeat my Salat (prayer) or wudu (because of doubts), then my wife will be like the back of my mother and swears for it about divorce.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is of the misdeeds of Satan. He does not owe anything because of it.’”
